log.msg: Findings. (1) 00:31 crash = JS, ours: LiveRefine calls VoicePage.raw() un-awaited; page_tools refused (no session f21bb81a... as dictate-red-tests used a fake id) -> rejected queue promise -> unhandled rejection -> reportOnUncaughtException report (header event Exception, message in javascriptStack) -> process exit -> Servex.shutdown() exit handler down() stopped every live agent (registry state stopped, stopped_by null) -> heap corruption 0xC0000374 in teardown 6 s later -> next boot revive() skips stopped rows -> revived []. (2) 01:24 crash = 0xC0000409 fast-fail, no JS handler ran, rows left working/idle, the 30-minute window revived 8. So the difference is whether the exit handler ran. Plan: down() writes a snapshot first, revive() accepts stopped rows listed there, crash without snapshot revives working/idle revivable rows with a live task past the window, VoicePage write never leaves an unhandled rejection, process-level unhandledRejection guard.

findings.text: `Server/ServexFence.mjs` and the new `FENCE_SERVEX=1` switch in `Server/Browser.mjs:66` are not indexed in `Server/readme.md` or `Server/doc/browser.md`. `browser.md` is the doc for "the one Chromium launcher", and it now has an env switch it doesn't mention. Two Dictate scripts still call `route.continue()`, against the new "fallback, never continue" rule (`Servex/doc/restart.md:68`, `core/Test/doc/health.md:38`): `ux/Dictate/test/stall.mjs:53` and `refresh.mjs:138`. The shutdown snapshot overwrites a `sustain --restart` snapshot whenever the exit handler runs (`Servex/Servex.js:1587`). The revived agent would then lose its "(asked by X)" note, because `Agents.js:513` drops `by` once `how` is set. `process.on("unhandledRejection")` (`Servex/Servex.js:1603`) changes Node's default from "crash" to "log and continue" for all of Servex. That's a reasonable call and it's documented. Watch `servex.jsonl` for `unhandled_rejection` events piling up silently.

Memory check (vscode-mastermind asked): the monitor DOES log ram_free_gb once a minute (system.jsonl, type minute). Joined to all 19 crashes in crashes.jsonl (10-20..11-02): free RAM at the crash had median ~5.3 GB against a baseline median 7.6 GB (p5 4.1); the first three crashes had 15-16 GB free; only one (10-25 06:32) was near exhaustion (0.5 GB); 11-02 00:31 and 01:24 had 2.6/2.4 GB (the baseline p25 is 6.5, so low but not out). Node process count at the crash rose from 14-20 (10-21) to 164-165 (11-02). So physical RAM is not a sufficient trigger (3 of 3 early crashes had plenty); memory pressure is a plausible contributor lately, and commit charge (the 93% reading) is not sampled, so it cannot be tested from the logs. Proposal: add commit_pct to the minute line. Not proved either way.

findings.text: If Servex crashes again during the stagger, every agent still waiting in the queue is lost. For each queued agent, the registry row keeps the boot id of the dying Servex until `reopen()` runs. The next boot only revives rows where `row.boot === prev.boot` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:475`), so it buries those agents as "not open in the previous boot". With 17 agents and a 3 s gap, the queue takes 48 s to drain. The 09:47 crash came 62 s after a boot, which is exactly the case this change exists for. Fix: before queueing (`Agents.js:526`, `:536`), stamp each queued row with `this.boot`, or include the queued ids in a snapshot, and add a check 5 to `crash-revive.test.mjs` that boots twice in a row.

The task folder doesn't record this work, so a fresh agent couldn't continue from it. `session.jsonl` ends with the landing of `ac587d301` (09:09Z), and nothing in `session.jsonl` or `inbox.jsonl` mentions the stagger. The commits `02fe5aaaa` and `c6ee98e6b` sit unmerged on `worktree/servex-revive-stagger`. Add a log line, or a child task, that names the branch, the ask behind it and its merge state.

The "Crash and revive" section of `Servex/readme.md` (line 54) doesn't mention the stagger or `SERVEX_REVIVE_GAP_S`; only `doc/restart.md:65` does. Add half a sentence plus the link, so someone searching the env var finds it from the readme.

The `revive` line in `servex.jsonl` (`Agents.js:550`) lists every queued agent under `revived` and `told` before any of them has been reopened. A failure shows up later as a separate `revive-failed` line. `restart.md:65` says this, but anything that counts revives from the `revive` line will overcount.
I checked the race where a message arrives during the gap: `send()` → `wake()` reopens the agent, and the later `start()` finds it live and only tells it (`Agents.js:517-518`). That one is handled.
Tests in the stagger worktree: `node Servex/agents/crash-revive.test.mjs` passes 15 checks and `revive-sweep.test.mjs` passes 4. Neither runs in a gate.

The task folder still does not record the stagger work, as the last review's finding 2 said: `session.jsonl` has no line naming `worktree/servex-revive-stagger` (head `04581354c`, unmerged), the ask behind it or its merge state, so a fresh agent could not continue from this folder. Add one log line (or a child task) with the branch, the reason (the 09:47 crash 62 s after a 6-agent revive) and "awaiting merge".

An agent the owner stops while it waits in the revive queue comes back anyway: `stop()` on a row that is not live only marks it `stopped` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:882-884`), but the queued `go()` calls `start()`, which reopens from the `row` it captured at boot (`Agents.js:519`) and never re-reads it, and `snapshot()` keeps listing it from `this.reviving` (`Agents.js:570`). Fix: in `go()`, skip the agent when its row now has `stopped_by` (or have `stop()` delete it from `this.reviving`), and add a check to `crash-revive.test.mjs`.

The last review's finding 1 is fixed: queued rows are re-stamped with the live boot before the queue starts (`Agents.js:537-541`), `snapshot()` lists the queue, and check 5 in `crash-revive.test.mjs` boots twice and gets all three back. In the worktree, `crash-revive.test.mjs` passes 20 checks and `revive-sweep.test.mjs` passes 4.
The last review's finding 3 is fixed: `Servex/readme.md:56` now names `SERVEX_REVIVE_GAP_S`, its default and the mid-turn-first order.

The `revive` line in `servex.jsonl` still counts queued agents as `revived` before they start (`Agents.js:557`). `restart.md:65` says so; a `queued` list beside `revived` would make the line honest without needing the doc.

log.text: Follow-up (vscode-mastermind, 2026-11-02 09:50 UTC): the 09:47 native crash came 62 s after a boot that revived 6 agents at once, and ended on a burst of /mcp posts. Checked all 20 trails in crashes.jsonl against 43,000 ten-second windows of crumbs.log: bursts of the same size (38 and 31 /mcp posts per 2 s) happened on boots that then ran 6406 s and 2135 s, and 4 of the 13 crashes since request crumbs began were idle. So /mcp bursts are not shown to be the trigger (doc/restart.md). Built the cheap mitigation anyway on branch worktree/servex-revive-stagger (head ac6970093, merge pending): Agents.revive reopens agents one every SERVEX_REVIVE_GAP_S seconds (default 3, 0 = all at once), mid-turn first. Alternative: stagger at the spawn gate (Servex.admission) with a min-interval check; not chosen because a resume is deliberately never held and the queue is drained only on the monitor tick.
